Article Title: Chita Andolan is back: Why are Madhya Pradesh's Panna villagers protesting against Ken-Betwa project
Article Text:
MP dam project: Protesters brave rain and waterlogging for 20th day

What is happening in Madhya Pradesh's Panna?

Several women and other protesters had fallen ill after staying in water and rain for several days, with some suffering from wounds on their feet and other skin-related problems. (ANI photo)

So why are the protesters back?

For thousands of tribal families living in the path of the project, it has become a battle over land, forests, livelihoods and identity.

Affected families have staged some of the country's most striking demonstrations, standing waist-deep in river water, laying beside symbolic funeral pyres and even climbed symbolic gallows.

'Ken-Betwa River Linking Project' is India's first river-linking initiative aimed to transform the drought-prone Bundelkhand region through irrigation, drinking water supply and power generation.

What is the project aiming to accomplish?

Remember the unnerving visuals from Chita Andolan in Madhya Pradesh? Displaced Tribals sleeping on pyres, standing in water for their compensation. The unique protest is back and in its 20th day with agitators battling rain, waterlogging, lathicharge and general apathy by the authorities.Activist Amit Bhatnagar, Jai Kisan Sangathan leader, who has been on a hunger strike for the past four days, was arrested on Wednesday as protesters demonstrated chita, jal, sooli, mitti, bhook (pyre, water, gallows, soil, hunger) other forms of satyagraha.Bhatnagar accused the Panna administration of suppressing the agitation by lathicharging protesters, including women.Speaking to TOI before his arrest, Bhatnagar said, "For the past three days, the police have been bringing along people dressed in plain clothes, who misbehaved with women, entered their homes and even took away people’s phones which have still not been returned. When we approach the police, they ask who took the phones. How are people supposed to identify every face and find out who took them?""There is an atmosphere of fear in the villages. If we say anything, they start resorting to lathi-charge and filing false cases against the protesters," he added.“I am courting arrest because democracy is being murdered. Are we not even allowed to protest peacefully? We are putting ourselves through hardship to raise our concerns, but instead of listening to us, they have cut off the electricity and water. Even the British never did this. ”The latest protest follows a 15-day agitation in July, led largely by tribal women, after which the administration had assured protesters that eligible and genuinely displaced families would be transparently included in compensation and rehabilitation lists.However, the protesters claimed that they did not get the promised compensation. Also, their houses were now inundated, with two to three feet of water entering homes in several villages which now stand waterlogged including Mandalia, Tapariya and Kuwarpur."The families whose houses have been submerged are so poor that they have been forced to continue living there, or put up one makeshift shelter next to another, and then another. Earlier, the water would rise by half a foot at a time. But this time there was heavy rain on the 26th and 27th of September, followed by a 24-hour red alert, leaving them with no time to move. The villages turned into islands,” said Bhatnagar.The protesters claim that the compensation process remains incomplete, with several families receiving only Rs 5 lakh despite the government announcing a Rs 12.5-lakh package.They are also opposing the compensation conditions, which makes several tribals ineligible for relief.“The cut-off date under Section 11 has been set as 2018, which means people who are now 25-26 years old have received nothing. Those who are older are getting only Rs 5 lakh. What are families with eight or 10 children supposed to do?" asked Bhatnagar, adding that they were not against development projects, but that this development should not come at the cost of the rights of tribals.Bhatnagar pointed to Section 38 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, which he said raised concerns about any displacement or submergence taking place before compensation and rehabilitation obligations had been fulfilled.“Villages and homes are now submerged. Houses have started collapsing and water has entered them. Yet, Section 38 of the 2013 law says that compensation for an irrigation project should be paid six months before submergence. If the houses were submerged two months ago, compensation should have been paid eight months earlier,” he said.The authorities, on the other hand, claim that they have been conducting fresh surveys and distributing compensation to affected families. TOI reached out to Chhatarpur district magistrate and is still awaiting a response from the administration.The Majhgawan dam project aims to transfer surplus water from Ken river to Betwa through the Daudhan Dam, a network of tunnels and a 221-km canal. It is supposed to address water shortages in drought-prone Bundelkhand region that spans across Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.The project traces back to a plan introduced in 1980 and cleared in 2021 to connect the rivers. Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid its foundation stone in December 2024.The project is expected to improve agricultural output, curb migration and strengthen groundwater recharge through the revival of traditional Chandela-era ponds.
Article Summary: Mp dam project: protesters brave rain and waterlogging for 20th day. Affected families have staged some of the country's most striking demonstrations. Several women and other protesters had fallen ill after staying in water and rain for several days.

Article Title: Ram Temple donation row: SC to hear plea against Champat Rai on Nov 2 over alleged irregularities
Article Text:
The Supreme Court has agreed to hear on November 2 a plea filed by the Akhil Bharat Hindu Mahasabha seeking legal action against former Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust general secretary Champat Rai

What is the case?

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday agreed to hear on November 2 plea filed by the Akhil Bharat Hindu Mahasabha seeking legal action against former Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust general secretary Champat Rai and others over alleged irregularities in donations and land transactions linked to the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.According to news agency ANI, the plea alleges that donations collected for the construction of the temple were misappropriated and that land was illegally purchased in areas surrounding the temple.The plea also seeks the dissolution of the existing Trust and its complete reconstitution.A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said the petition would be taken up along with other pending pleas concerning the same.Earlier, Rai had been given a clean chit by the UP-State SIT, which probed the donation theft. He is listed in the chargesheet as a key prosecution witness. Chargesheet names as accused only eight arrested counting agents and employees for criminal breach of trust and corruption.Rai informed investigators that he first learned of the irregularities via a phone call and video message while travelling. He subsequently reviewed CCTV footage and suggested lodging the formal police complaint.The alleged misappropriation of donations at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya has triggered a political and administrative controversy. The issue came to light on June 7, when former Samajwadi Party MLA Pawan Pandey alleged that around Rs 7-7.5 crore from the daily offerings made by devotees had been siphoned off. He alleged that people associated with the temple’s management were involved in the alleged misappropriation.The allegations soon gained political traction after SP chief Akhilesh Yadav backed the claims and sought accountability. A section of local BJP leaders also called for an investigation, putting the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, which manages the temple, under increased scrutiny.The concerns grew after Nripendra Misra, chairman of the temple construction committee and a trust member, flagged loopholes in the existing system for handling and counting cash donations. He recommended appointing a professional CEO to strengthen oversight and transparency.Trust general secretary Champat Rai initially rejected the allegations. However, amid mounting scrutiny, the trust sought an investigation by the Uttar Pradesh government.The SIT submitted an interim report within a week, flagging procedural weaknesses in the system used to manage temple donations and recommending structural reforms to strengthen monitoring and accountability.The probe subsequently led to arrests in connection with the alleged irregularities.
Article Summary: The supreme court has agreed to hear on november 2 a plea filed by the akhil bharat hindu mahasabha seeking legal action against former shri ram janmabhoomi teerth kshetra trust general secretary champat rai. The plea alleges that donations collected for the construction of the temple were misappropriated and that land was illegally purchased.

Article Title: Hate speech case: Mahua Moitra’s interim protection from arrest extended till January 2027
Article Text:
Mahua Moitra's interim protection from arrest extended

NEW DELHI: The Calcutta high court on Thursday extended till January 29, 2027, the interim protection granted to Mahua Moitra , MP from the Mamata Banerjee-led faction of the Trinamool Congress (TMC), in an alleged hate speech case.During the hearing, West Bengal advocate general Surojit Nath Mitra, appearing for the state government, submitted a report before the single-judge bench of Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya. The report noted that Moitra appeared before the Hogalberia police station in Nadia district on August 14 and answered the questions put to her by the investigating officer, in compliance with the court's earlier directions.The report further stated that the investigation into the alleged hate speech was still underway.Moitra's counsel told the court that the Krishnanagar MP was not subjected to egg pelting when she appeared at the police station on August 14. The lawyer had earlier alleged that Moitra faced such attacks whenever she visited her constituency in Nadia district.After hearing both sides, Justice Bhattacharyya extended Moitra's interim protection from coercive action in the case until January 29, 2027.The court fixed January 13 as the next date of hearing.In the petition, the TMC Mamata faction leader, has sought quashing of the criminal proceedings initiated against her in connection with the case registered at Hogalberia police station on the complaint of a BJP worker. She has alleged that the case is based on “concocted and motivated allegations”.On July 21, Justice Bhattacharyya had granted Moitra interim protection from coercive action in the case and directed her to appear before the investigating officer on August 14 for questioning.The court had ordered that no coercive action be taken against her until October 5, subject to her complying with the conditions imposed by the court.Acting on a plea by her counsel, the judge had also directed the police to ensure that Moitra was not subjected to egg pelting when she appeared before the investigating officer.
Article Summary: Mahua moitra's interim protection from arrest extended till january 29, 2027. Tmc mamata faction leader has sought quashing of criminal proceedings initiated against her. She has alleged that the case is based on ‘concocted and motivated allegations’

SC refuses TMC plea to operate four debit-frozen bank accounts

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday dismissed a plea by the Mamata Banerjee-led TMC faction seeking permission to operate four debit-frozen bank accounts, declining to interfere with a Calcutta High Court order that had rejected the request.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale noted that the Election Commission has frozen the party symbol and that the larger question of who is entitled to the funds in the accounts remains pending adjudication."We refrain from going into the merits. We are not inclined to exercise our jurisdiction under Article 136. We request high court to expedite the hearing," the bench said.The TMC had sought permission to operate four accounts with public sector banks that were debit-frozen by the West Bengal Police, arguing that the FIRs related to the freeze contained procedural lapses.Separately, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) has frozen Rs 440 crore in three accounts held by the party with HDFC Bank as part of its investigation into the alleged laundering of Rs 160 crore in party funds through Kolkata-based Carewell Aviation.The agency alleges that the funds were used to purchase an Embraer Legacy 600 aircraft and an Agusta helicopter for Rs 112 crore through what it described as dubious transactions.The ED said the aircraft and helicopter were later rented to the TMC, with substantial amounts transferred on the pretext of their use.“The Embraer Legacy 600 aircraft and Agusta helicopter were rented to TMC itself, even though they were purchased from the corpus of the party, and substantial amounts were transferred on the pretext of aircraft usage. The above stated dubious arrangement is under probe to ascertain the actual beneficial purpose of the transactions,” the ED said.The Calcutta High Court on August 27 had refused to pass an interim order allowing the Mamata Banerjee-led TMC faction to operate four debit-frozen bank accounts holding around Rs 804 crore. It had observed that granting such relief would undermine its earlier order allowing the political party to meet its day-to-day expenses.

Article Title: ‘Many are in contact’: Akhilesh claims BJP alliance MLAs in touch with SP ahead of Rajya Sabha polls
Article Text:
File photo: Samajwadi Party National President Akhilesh Yadav (Picture credit: PTI)

SP sticks to alliance, winnability formula

Rajya Sabha contest heats up

Yadav defends Nathwani candidature

Sugarcane payments and Raebareli remarks

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday claimed that several MLAs from the ruling BJP-led alliance in Uttar Pradesh are in contact with his party ahead of the Rajya Sabha elections, while saying the SP would not make commitments it could not honour.“There are many who are in contact. But how do we adjust them? We do not want to make a promise and then go back on it,” Yadav said at a press conference at the SP office.The remarks came as the SP formally entered the Rajya Sabha contest in Uttar Pradesh, with party candidates Professor Ram Gopal Yadav and Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani filing their nomination papers. Akhilesh Yadav accompanied both candidates during the filing.Asked about the party's plans for next year's Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls, Yadav said the alliance that existed earlier would continue. On seat-sharing, he reiterated that the SP would use winnability as the basis for deciding which party contests a seat.“The SP has said this earlier and I am saying it again -- winnability is the basis for a seat,” he said.The Election Commission has announced that polling for 11 Rajya Sabha seats, 10 from Uttar Pradesh and one from Uttarakhand, will be held on October 16.The terms of the sitting members from the two states are due to expire on November 25.Yadav said the democratic system requires representatives to be elected by the people and lawmakers to subsequently elect members of the Upper House.“Democracy should not have dishonesty. Had the BJP not indulged in dishonesty, the SP would have had three Rajya Sabha MPs,” he said, referring to the previous Rajya Sabha election in which SP candidate Alok Ranjan lost after cross-voting.Yadav said the SP was now urging MLAs to use the opportunity to “wash away the past”.Uttar Pradesh deputy chief minister Keshav Prasad Maurya , however, claimed that 25 SP MLAs were in touch with the BJP.“We will surprise them. 25 of their MLAs are in touch with us,” Maurya said, according to news agency ANI.His remarks came after the SP announced Ram Gopal Yadav and Nathwani as its two candidates.Uttar Pradesh minister and Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party chief Om Prakash Rajbhar also questioned whether the SP's candidates reflected its PDA — Pichhada, Dalit and Alpashankhyak — formulation.He cautioned the party against attempting to secure a third seat at the risk of losing its second.Defending the nomination of industrialist Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani, Yadav said he was pleased that the SP had the opportunity to send a representative of the younger generation and a “new way of thinking” to the Rajya Sabha.“The SP has decided to connect with the industrial sector and therefore, to make someone associated with the industry its Rajya Sabha member,” he said.Responding to criticism over backing an industrialist, Yadav said, “I think you should read about socialism again. I will give you a book by (Ram Manohar) Lohia.”He said socialist thought also focused on prosperity and equality and argued that governments across the country seek investment to drive economic growth.Yadav said the SP wanted to promote industries and employment in Uttar Pradesh, adding that the party would support those who contribute to economic growth, farmer employment and jobs for young people.Yadav also promised that sugarcane growers would receive pending payments within 24 to 48 hours if the SP formed the government in Uttar Pradesh. He said the party's election manifesto would include several measures for farmers.On his recent visit to Raebareli and allegations of police misconduct involving SP MLA Rahul Lodhi, Yadav questioned how police could behave in such a manner with an elected representative.“How can police behave like this with an elected representative?” he asked.He also said, “This time, it will be Lodhi versus (Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister) Yogi (Adityanath).”Yadav further said Uttar Pradesh's proposed target of becoming a USD 1-trillion economy could not be achieved through corruption, saying, “A USD-1-trillion economy will not be built through theft of offerings.”He also said the SP would continue to focus on farmers, recalling former prime minister Chaudhary Charan Singh and farmer leader Mahendra Singh Tikait.
Article Summary: Samajwadi party chief akhilesh yadav claims that several mlas from the ruling bjp-led alliance in uttar pradesh are in contact with his party. Yadav said the sp would not make commitments it could not honour. The election commission has announced that polling for 11 rajya sabha seats will be held on october 16.

Article Title: Delhi riots case: High court rejects bail pleas Of Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam
Article Text:
Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam denied bail by high court

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has refused to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots.Senior Advocate Trideep Pais, appearing for Umar Khalid, submitted that there had been three “small changes in circumstances” since the earlier proceedings. He also referred the court to a Supreme Court judgment in support of his submissions.Pais pointed out that charges have not yet been framed in the case and, consequently, prosecution witnesses are yet to be examined. The court also noted that the charges were yet to be framed.Pais further submitted that a Special Leave Petition (SLP) is pending before the Supreme Court and that the trial court has indicated it would await the Supreme Court’s order. He then continued his submissions by referring to the Supreme Court judgment.Khalid and Imam had approached the Delhi High Court earlier this year after their bail applications were dismissed by the trial court for the third time on July 4. Imam was arrested in the case on August 25, 2020, while Khalid was arrested on September 13, 2020.The Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots, PTI reported.The police argued that they could not seek bail on parity with other co-accused, stating that the Supreme Court had earlier categorised them as being part of the “command authority” and held that their “risk profiles” justified “continuing detention”.The police also argued that the present bail pleas were in the teeth of the Supreme Court’s January 5 order, which directed them to seek release only after the examination of protected witnesses was completed or after one year, whichever was earlier.On July 4, the trial court rejected Khalid’s bail application, saying it had “no option but to follow” the Supreme Court’s January 5 order and could therefore neither entertain the plea nor grant him relief.On September 2, 2025, a Delhi High Court division bench denied bail to Khalid and Imam. The Supreme Court upheld the verdict on January 5 but granted relief to co-accused Gulfisha Fatima, Meeran Haider, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohammad Saleem Khan and Shadab Ahmad.A bench of Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice NV Anjaria had observed that there was a prima facie case against Khalid and Imam under the UAPA.On May 22, the Supreme Court granted six months’ interim bail to co-accused Abdul Khalid Saifi and Tasleem Ahmad, while referring to a larger bench the issue of prolonged incarceration of undertrials under the UAPA due to the stringent conditions for granting bail.
Article Summary: Umar khalid, sharjeel imam denied bail by high court in uapa case related to 2020 delhi riots. Delhi police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were ‘masterminds’ of the riots.

Article Title: What makes a rape case 'rarest of rare'? How courts decide on the death penalty
Article Text:
Should death penalty remain exception in rape cases, not the rule?

And should death remain an exception rather than the rule?

Why women's safety is back at the centre of debate

2026 witness​es shocking incidents of sexual assault

When does rape become 'rarest of rare'?

Activist Yogita Bhayana in conversation with TOI

What changes when the accused is a minor?

Minor victims in rape cases in India: NCRB data

Does a harsher sentence always mean justice?

Two cases with different court sentences

Why tougher laws alone may not be enough

Delhi University students take out protest march amid rains to Miranda House college in north campus over women safety after Kalkaji gang rape.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Every time a brutal rape case shocks the country, the demand returns almost immediately: give the harshest possible punishment.The anger is understandable. But the law applies a much narrower test. Not every rape case, however grave, crosses the threshold for the death penalty.India recorded 29,536 rape cases in 2024, according to the latest National Crime Records Bureau data. In Delhi, 1,058 rape cases were registered that year, while Delhi Police reported 1,901 cases in 2025.The figures come amid renewed attention on sexual violence, with a series of recent cases in Delhi and across the country bringing questions of punishment, deterrence and justice back into focus.While Indian law provides for stringent punishment, including the death penalty in certain rape cases, capital punishment remains restricted to specific circumstances.So when does a rape case cross the legal threshold for the ultimate punishment? What makes one case “rarest of rare”, while another results in life imprisonment?A series of recent cases has once again put women’s safety under scrutiny.In September, a 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by three men posing as police personnel at Astha Kunj Park near Kalkaji Mandir in Delhi. The case triggered student protests demanding stronger measures for women’s safety, and police arrested the accused.In August, another 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by a bus driver and conductor after boarding a bus from Greater Noida. She was later dropped near Kashmere Gate. The National Human Rights Commission took suo motu cognisance of the case and sought reports from authorities.Against this backdrop, the Supreme Court on Monday took suo motu cognisance of recent rape incidents in Delhi-NCR, flagging what it described as a "systematic failure" to ensure basic public safety.Concerns have extended beyond Delhi.In Bihar, three incidents involving alleged sexual harassment and assault were reported within days. In Jamui, a teenage boy and girl were allegedly stopped and assaulted by a group of men on September 19, with three accused arrested after a video surfaced online. In Samastipur, a minor girl was allegedly assaulted and molested, while another case in Banka’s Mandar Hill area involved allegations of a woman being harassed and her male friend assaulted.The cases have also spilled onto the streets. Students and young people in the national capital are holding protests demanding safer public spaces, stronger policing and greater accountability.Indian law permits the death penalty in certain aggravated rape cases, including those involving minors and cases where the victim dies or is left in a persistent vegetative state, under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the POCSO Act.But the existence of the death penalty does not mean it follows automatically in the most brutal cases.Advocate Sumit Nagpal said courts consider factors including the brutality of the offence, injuries caused, the vulnerability of the survivor and the long-term consequences while determining punishment.Rupali Jain, who practises in the high court and Supreme Court, said the harm caused by rape, while grave, cannot by itself justify capital punishment."As harm is inherent in every rape, it cannot alone justify death. The court must also apply the 'criminal test', the offender’s age, antecedents, background, custodial conduct and prospects of reform, as reiterated in Manoj v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2022)," she said.The "rarest of rare" doctrine gained renewed attention following the 2012 Nirbhaya case . On December 16, 2012, a 23-year-old woman was gang-raped and brutally assaulted inside a moving bus in Delhi. She died from her injuries days later.Four adult accused were sentenced to death by the trial court in 2013. The Delhi high court upheld the punishment in 2014, and the Supreme Court confirmed the death sentences in 2017, holding that the case fell within the “rarest of rare” category.However, the Supreme Court has also held that the brutality or heinousness of an offence alone does not automatically make it a "rarest of rare" case. Courts must weigh aggravating circumstances against mitigating factors, including the possibility of reform and rehabilitation.But the death penalty is not automatic, even in cases involving extreme violence.The Bilkis Bano case offers another example of how courts apply the 'rarest of rare' test differently.In the Bilkis Bano case, 11 men were convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment for gang rape, murder and other offences linked to the 2002 Gujarat riots. Bilkis was 21 and five months pregnant when she was raped, and several members of her family were killed.The case shows why the "rarest of rare" test is not based only on how brutal or shocking a crime appears. Courts must also consider other factors, including the background of the accused and whether there is any possibility of reform.Activist Yogita Bhayana, however, argues that the impact of rape on the survivor should receive greater weight when courts consider the threshold."Every rape case is rarest of the rare in terms of the victim," she said, arguing that the legal system can focus heavily on physical brutality while overlooking the lasting impact on survivors.Bhayana said she believes the death penalty should remain available in rape cases and argued for greater weight to be given to the consequences of the crime for survivors while deciding punishment.Jain, too, stressed the need for severe punishment, while emphasising that its deterrent effect depends on certainty and speed of enforcement."In my opinion, the most effective way to deter sexual violence is stern punishment, imposed swiftly and with certainty. The offender must know that the consequence is severe and unavoidable: imprisonment for the remainder of natural life and, in the rarest of cases, death. The statute already provides for this, as Sections 65, 66, 70 and 71 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 prescribe natural-life imprisonment or death for the gravest forms. The deficit lies in enforcement."The legal process changes significantly when the accused is under 18.Under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, a child aged between 16 and 18 who is accused of a “heinous offence”, including rape, can undergo a preliminary assessment by the Juvenile Justice Board.The Board looks at the child’s mental and physical capacity to commit the offence, whether they understood its consequences and the circumstances in which the alleged offence took place.Depending on that assessment, the case can be transferred to the Children’s Court, which then decides whether the child should be tried as an adult.Rupali Jain said the existing law already provides a framework for dealing with serious offences committed by juveniles, and the focus should remain on how it is implemented rather than simply lowering the age threshold.She also pointed out that the Juvenile Justice Act bars the death penalty and life imprisonment without the possibility of release for a child in conflict with law.However, activist Yogita Bhayana argues that the distinction between different degrees of brutality can be deeply troubling for survivors.“The miner will be treated as miner unless he brutally kills her, rape her in a very gruesome manner. Then otherwise, it will not be in the rarest of the rare category. So we need to change the whole thing,” she said, arguing that the system should focus more closely on the impact of the crime on the survivor and called for greater awareness and stronger mechanisms to deal with sexual offences.For survivors, justice does not necessarily end with an arrest, conviction or sentence.Activist Yogita Bhayana said the distinction between "high-profile" and ordinary rape cases often comes from media attention rather than the nature of the crime or the survivor’s experience."There is no case which is high profile. What becomes media-highlighted becomes high profile," she said, pointing out that even Nirbhaya came from a humble, lower-middle-class family.She said survivors often continue to deal with trauma, repeated questioning and the pressures of the legal process long after public attention has moved on."Attention doesn’t mean justice," Bhayana said.Dr Vinodh Sreeram, senior psychiatrist & addiction specialist at Maarga Mind Care, Bengaluru, said rape can deeply alter a survivor’s sense of safety, relationships and ability to return to everyday life.He cautioned against judging trauma only by visible injuries or by how brutal an assault appears. Two survivors of similar incidents can experience very different psychological effects depending on factors such as age, past experiences, their relationship with the accused and the support available to them."The absence of visible injury should never be mistaken for the absence of psychological trauma," he said.On whether the death penalty can provide psychological closure, Sreeram said there is no single answer. Some survivors or families may see a severe sentence as justice, but "closure rarely comes from the sentence alone".Being believed, treated with dignity, protected from further harm and supported through recovery can be just as important, he said. Repeated questioning, cross-examination, delays and prolonged appeals can themselves become additional sources of distress.Recent protests in Delhi have again brought demands for safer public spaces, stronger policing, better surveillance and greater accountability to the forefront.Advocate Sumit Nagpal said the biggest challenge is not necessarily the absence of laws, but the capacity to enforce them."The bottleneck is capacity, not the statute. India has roughly twenty judges per million people against a recommended fifty, and police strength sits well below sanctioned levels in most states. Until that gap closes, every reform stays on paper," he said."So the real agenda is unglamorous: more investigators, more courts, more forensic capacity, fewer vacancies. No amendment will substitute for that."Activist Yogita Bhayana said the biggest gap remains implementation. While reforms, awareness and gender-sensitisation efforts have increased, she said survivors continue to face inadequate support, delays in fast-track courts and a lack of sensitivity within the system.She also warned that repeated exposure to sexual-violence cases can make institutions become "immune" to such crimes."For them, they see it like an everyday thing," she said, arguing that continued training and sensitisation are needed to ensure sexual violence is not treated as routine.Dr Vinodh Sreeram said debates around harsher punishment must also account for the realities of reporting, particularly because many survivors know the accused and may face fear, stigma and family pressure.A trauma-informed justice system, he said, should focus on sensitive questioning, privacy, timely trials and access to psychological support.“Justice is not only about the severity of punishment. It is also about ensuring that survivors are heard, protected, treated with dignity and given the opportunity to rebuild their lives,” Sreeram said.The death penalty is only one part of the debate. The larger challenge is to prevent such crimes, ensure quicker justice and make sure survivors get the support they need.
Article Summary: India recorded 29,536 rape cases in 2024, according to the latest national crime records bureau data. In delhi, 1,058 rape cases were registered that year, while delhi police reported 1,901 cases in 2025. Figures come amid renewed attention on sexual violence, with a series of recent cases in delhi and across the country.

Article Title: Monsoon deficit at 13%, officially a drought year
Article Text:

Winter rain may bring relief to southern India

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you believe is the best solution for dealing with drought conditions? NEW DELHI: The rainy season in India technically ended on Wednesday, with the summer (southwest) monsoon rainfall during June-Sept period recording a deficit of nearly 13% - a level of shortfall which is considered a drought. Significantly, this is the fourth lowest seasonal rainfall since 2001 and the 13th lowest since 1901.The situation is likely to be better during winter when northeast monsoon hits south Peninsular India between Oct 15 and Oct 21, with the IMD predicting 'normal' rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema region, Kerala and south interior Karnataka during Oct-Dec period. However, the winter monsoon will bring cheer to limited regions.Though most other parts of India are expected to receive 'below-normal' rainfall during the Oct-Dec period, some areas of northwest India (Punjab, parts of Haryana, Uttarakhand, Himachal and J&K) and southern parts of peninsular India are likely to get "normal to above-normal" rainfall. Incidentally, Punjab and peninsular India had to face huge rainfall deficit during the summer monsoon season, which led to drought in many districts.Overall, south Peninsular India receives 30% of its annual rainfall during northeast (winter) monsoon season. TN, Puducherry and Karaikal receive 48% of their annual rainfall during northeast monsoon season. So, normal winter monsoon this year may bring relief to the region, which received the fourth lowest summer monsoon rainfall since 1901.“We cannot forecast exact date of arrival of winter monsoon in south Peninsula at this stage. It generally coincides with final withdrawal of summer monsoon and may hit the region any day during Oct 15-21,” said IMD chief Mrutyunjay Mohapatra. Though India as a whole received nearly 13% less than normal rainfall, east and northeast India faced the highest deficit of 25%, followed by south Peninsula (24%), northwest India (6%) and central India (3%). Mohapatra said there has been a recent trend of east & northeast India consistently reporting decrease in rainfall.
Article Summary: Winter rain may bring relief to southern india. Imd predicts 'normal' rainfall over tamil nadu, puducherry, karaikal, coastal andhra pradesh and rayalaseema region. Punjab and peninsular india had to face huge rainfall deficit during the summer monsoon season, which led to drought in many districts.

Article Title: Money laundering case: NIA court orders charges against Yasin Malik, six others

NEW DELHI: A special National Investigation Agency (NIA) court has directed that charges be framed against separatist Yasin Malik and six other accused under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) for allegedly receiving foreign funding from the Pakistani establishment through hawala channels.The other accused are Zahoor Ahmed Shah Watali, Abdul Rashid Sheikh, Shabir Ahmad Shah, Naval Kishore Kapoor, Trison Farms and Construction Pvt Ltd, and Masarat Alam Bhat.Special NIA Judge Prashant Sharma ordered that charges be framed after considering the material against the accused."I conclude that prima facie, there is sufficient material on record based upon which strong suspicion is raised against all seven accused persons, namely Zahoor Ahmad Shah Watali, Naval Kishore Kapoor, M/s Trison Farms and Constructions Pvt Ltd, Mohd. Yasin Malik, Shabir Ahmad Shah, Masarat Alam and Abdul Rashid Sheikh, for which said accused persons have to be charged with offence u/sec. 3 of PMLA, punishable u/sec. 4 of PMLA," the Special Judge ordered on Wednesday.The investigation conducted by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) found that the scheduled offences generated proceeds of crime amounting to Rs. 8,94,87,639, which were allegedly received, routed, transferred, concealed, possessed, acquired and/or used by the accused through various channels.The court noted that, according to the NIA's second supplementary chargesheet, Malik received Rs. 15,75,595 from Saudi Arabia. It said Malik received foreign funds totalling Rs. 30,75,595 as alleged proceeds of crime.The ED case is based on an NIA case registered in 2017.The agency alleged that Malik, then head of the Jammu & Kashmir Liberation Front (JKLF), received foreign funds through Zahoor Ahmad Shah Watali, along with Shabir Ahmad Shah and Masarat Alam, during 2015-16.According to the ED, emails linked to Malik showed that he had established a network to raise funds abroad, which were used to support the JKLF and carry out secessionist activities and violence in Jammu and Kashmir.The ED also alleged that the money was routed through cash couriers who collected funds from the Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi and delivered them to Hurriyat leaders, including Malik.

Article Title: ‘Might as well disband you’: SC slams UP police for cover-up job
Article Text:
A bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva asked why the state police should not be disbanded in view of its functioning.

How will people trust police: SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday slammed Uttar Pradesh police for not naming the accused in a road accident case despite the complainant catching him on the spot and handing him over to police. It said it would be better if investigations in all criminal cases were handed over to CBI if the state police worked with an agenda and did cover-up jobs.A bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva asked why the state police should not be disbanded in view of its functioning.“In everything you have an agenda. How will people trust you if this is how you proceed with matters? It is better if we ask the CBI to step in all UP police investigations. We might as well disband UP police. This nonsense has to stop at some point,” the court said.Supreme Court added that the affidavit filed by Shobhit Kumar, circle officer of Khurja in Bulandshahr, who was directed to give an explanation, was “utterly uninspiring”.“Toeing the line is one thing but bending over is another. And this kind of cover up job... less said the better,” SC said and summoned the officer to be present in court to give an explanation on his conduct.“The said officer shall be present before court on next date to account for the same. It would be open to him to file a better affidavit explaining as to why FIR No. 195/2026 was filed on Aug 19 against an unknown motorcycle rider when it is the admitted fact that the said rider was apprehended at the spot. In paragraph 6 of aforestated affidavit, the name of the motorcycle rider is disclosed as Tushar s/o Prempal. The reason as to why the name was left blank in the FIR initially and was, thereafter, supplemented, requires to be explained,” the bench said in its order.The bench sought an explanation on why an FIR was filed against unknown person in the case. “Why did you write unknown if the person was caught at the spot? Why did you register the FIR against an unknown motorcycle rider if he was caught on the spot? How will people trust the police?” the bench asked.
Article Summary: Supreme court slams uttar pradesh police for not naming the accused in a road accident case. It said it would be better if investigations in all criminal cases were handed over to cbi. A bench of justices sanjay kumar and sanjeev sachdeva asked why the state police should not be disbanded in view of its functioning.

NEW DELHI: Applying its recently framed policy of rejecting challenges to bails granted by high courts, Supreme Court on Wednesday told the West Bengal govt that it would dismiss the state's appeal against grant of interim bail to Milan Pradhan, Congress candidate for the Nandigram assembly bypoll, who is an accused in a 2007 murder case.A CJI-led bench expressed difficulty to list the matter on Thursday and said, "Instead of Thursday, we will dismiss the appeal on Monday."By Monday, electioneering for the bypoll would be over and the state's appeal would be infructuous. Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for the state, requested a bench headed by CJI Surya Kant for a hearing on Thursday of the appeal challenging the grant of interim bail to Pradhan for canvassing for the election scheduled for Oct 6, campaigning for which will end on Oct 4.When the bench said since the HC had granted only interim bail, it would not entertain such an appeal, Mehta brought up Pradhan's history sheet -- accused in a murder case and featuring in six other FIRs on serious crimes -- to request a hearing on Thursday.The HC had, citing the relief the SC gave to AAP leader Arvind Kejriwal, granted bail to Pradhan on Tuesday and asked him to surrender before the additional chief judicial magistrate, Haldia, on Oct 21.Counting of votes in Nandigram, which was vacated by chief minister Suvendu Adhikari who also won from Bhabanipur, will happen on Oct 9.The state said in its appeal, "The HC granted interim bail to Pradhan, an accused charged with multiple counts of heinous offences including murder, arson, bomb blasts and rioting with deadly weapons, solely on the untenable pretext of permitting him to participate in an election."It added, "The HC completely disregarded settled principles governing the grant of bail, overlooked the respondent's continuous evasion of judicial process for nearly two decades, ignored his active subversion of the criminal justice system, and exposed prosecution witnesses to imminent danger."

Article Title: Supreme Court allows sale, manufacture of next-generation green firecrackers
Article Text:
Government said manufacturers must comply with specifications/formulations tested and approved by the competent authority as well as with the prescribed noise limit and emission and safety requirements fixed under the law.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Ahead of the festive season, Supreme Court on Wednesday paved the way for the manufacture and sale of next-generation joined green firecrackers after Centre's recommendation. Commonly known as 'ladi', these were earlier banned by the court.SC also said a separate order would be passed for Delhi and indicated that while the bursting of firecrackers would not be banned, the activity would not be allowed at all hours.Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale that government had recommended that joined firecrackers, which complied with norms fixed by Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI), be allowed. The issue of using barium chemical remains undecided as the ASG told the bench that field trials were on, and sought time till Oct 15.Submitting the findings of CSIR-NEERI, Bhati said the report said 25 braids were burst in one second in conventional joined firecrackers whereas in next-generation joined firecrackers, only five braids were burst in a second.Government said manufacturers must comply with specifications/formulations tested and approved by the competent authority as well as with the prescribed noise limit and emission and safety requirements fixed under the law.Advocate Pranav Sachdeva, appearing for some manufacturers, assured the bench they would do so.As the pollution crisis in winter has become an annual affair in Delhi, the bench said it would pass a separate order for the national capital. "We're making this very clear. Neither are we going to agree with you for a total ban nor are we going to allow it 24 hours," the court said.A total ban would have a "sentimental effect", SC said, but allowing bursting of crackers throughout the day would have a "huge impact on every other living being, including old people, sick people and children"."We need to find a solution whereby we can give specified time and we can specify what crackers are to be used," the bench told the petitioner seeking curbs on the sale of firecrackers in NCR.Earlier, two government organisations had taken contradictory stands in SC on allowing next-generation green firecrackers. While CSIR-NEERI approved them saying their pollution levels had decreased by 40-60% and recommended commercial production of flowerpots, sparklers, 'chakkars', pencils, 'ladis' and twinkling stars, Central Pollution Control Board said they contained barium nitrate, which was banned by SC.
Article Summary: Government said manufacturers must comply with specifications/formulations tested and approved by the competent authority. Commonly known as 'ladi', these were earlier banned by the court. Sc also said a separate order would be passed for delhi and indicated that while the bursting of firecrackers would not be banned, the activity will not be allowed at all hours.

Article Title: Second full EC meet in 5 days, SIR extended again in Andhra Pradesh, Meghalaya
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The full Election Commission - comprising CEC Gyanesh Kumar and ECs S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi - met Wednesday, a second time in five days, and decided to extend the deadlines for the ongoing SIR exercise in Andhra Pradesh and Meghalaya, reports Bharti Jain.The revised period for disposal of claims and objections in Andhra will now run from July 31 to Oct 10. The date for publication of the final poll roll also stands extended to Oct 16. For Meghalaya, the date for publication of the final poll roll has been revised to Oct 26.The second full meeting of the commission since an Indian Express report alleged that ECs Sandhu and Joshi had objected to steps taken by EC on 14 occasions over 10 months reaffirms that the CEC and the two ECs have agreed to sit together and transact normal business of the commission through regular meetings.The draft roll of Meghalaya published on Aug 5 listed 21.7 lakh electors, with around 7.7% absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors deleted. In Andhra, the draft roll listed 3.7 crore electors after deleting 10.8% of its electorate.
Article Summary: The full election commission - comprising cec gyanesh kumar and ecs s s sandhu and vivek joshi - met wednesday, a second time in five days. The revised period for disposal of claims and objections in andhra will now run from july 31 to oct 10. The date for publication of the final poll roll also stands extended to oct 16.
